data.description:
## Problem

Several reconciler test helpers load engine modules by path with this pattern:

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    mod  = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)   # <-- does NOT replace an existing entry
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)        # <-- but execs into the NEW object
    return mod                          # <-- and returns the NEW object

When `sys.modules[name]` is already populated (another test file in the same worker loaded it first), `setdefault` keeps the OLD module object while the helper execs and returns a NEW one. Any engine module that then does `import mutation` resolves the OLD object, so the class the code constructs and the class the test asserts against are DIFFERENT objects with the same name.

Symptom, from CI (macos-latest, py3.13):

    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py::test_new_key_in_local_produces_outbound_create_mutation
    >   assert isinstance(m, mutation_mod.Mutation)
    E   AssertionError: assert False
    E    +  where False = isinstance(Mutation(direction=..., action=..., target='DSO-42'...), <class 'mutation.Mutation'>)

## Why it surfaced now

It is latent and ORDER-DEPENDENT, so it only fires when a particular pair of files lands in the same xdist worker. Change 1043 (story 2932) added tests, which changed sharding: patchset 1 passed CI, patchset 2 failed twice deterministically, with the only delta being added tests in an unrelated subsystem. The reconciler code itself is untouched by that change.

Not reproducible on a py3.14 local venv even running the whole `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/` directory in one process; the failing CI job is py3.13 on macos-latest. Treat CI as the reproducer.

## Fix

Make the helper return the module that is ACTUALLY registered, so exactly one class object exists per name:

    existing = sys.modules.get(name)
    if existing is not None and getattr(existing, '__file__', None) == str(path):
        return existing
    ... module_from_spec ...
    sys.modules[name] = mod        # assign, do not setdefault
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

The path guard matters: these names (`mutation`, `differ`, `applier`) are generic, so blindly reusing any same-named module could bind to something unrelated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] no reconciler test helper uses `sys.modules.setdefault` for by-path module loading: `grep -rn 'sys.modules.setdefault' tests/` is empty
- [ ] a test asserts the helper returns the SAME object on a second call for the same name+path (one class object per name)
- [ ] a test asserts a same-name/different-path load does NOT silently reuse the wrong module
- [ ] [operator-attested] CI is green on macos-latest/py3.13 for a change that previously reproduced the failure, evidenced by the Gerrit change id and its Verified +1 recorded in a comment
data.title: Reconciler test _load_module uses sys.modules.setdefault, yielding two class objects and order-dependent isinstance failures
